answer: Each agent is a vertex in a payment network, but voting power comes from tokens locked for 30 days, not from the number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand mirror identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To gain more influence, an attacker must buy and immobilize more tokens; a spiral of new identities adds no power, while acquiring extra voting weight ties up capital that cannot be spent during the lock.
